LESSON: COUNTING CONCRETE OBJECTS

Grade: PP1
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: NUMBERS
Topic 2.3: Counting concrete objects

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Counting concrete objects. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. count concrete objects 1-9 10 lessons numeracy skills and associating a group of objects with a number symbol
2. demonstrate one to one correspondence while counting concrete objects
3. enjoy counting concrete objects within their environment
4. appreciate the use of one to one correspondence in real life situations. counting.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. count concrete objects 1-9 10 lessons numeracy skills and associating a group of objects with a number symbol
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to count concrete objects 1-9 10 lessons numeracy skills and associating a group of objects with a number symbol. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. demonstrate one to one correspondence while counting concrete objects
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to demonstrate one to one correspondence while counting concrete objects. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. enjoy counting concrete objects within their environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to enjoy counting concrete objects within their environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. appreciate the use of one to one correspondence in real life situations. counting.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to appreciate the use of one to one correspondence in real life situations. counting. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Counting concrete objects.
2. Explain Counting concrete objects to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Counting concrete objects.
4. Show that you can: count concrete objects 1-9 10 lessons numeracy skills and associating a group of objects with a number symbol
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Counting concrete objects. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Counting concrete objects important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. count concrete objects 1-9 10 lessons numeracy skills and associating a group of objects with a number symbol
2. demonstrate one to one correspondence while counting concrete objects
3. enjoy counting concrete objects within their environment
4. appreciate the use of one to one correspondence in real life situations. counting.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
